message:
Sounds like a good idea, Chris, and I'd be happy to do it -- give me a few days to get it together, and maybe I'll even be able to contextualize it for others and myself; to say, "This text helps me see this, and this other one helps me see that."

I encountered *Ways with Words* several years ago in a poorly run methods seminar (not at my current institution), before I'd fully articulated to myself my interest in class, so a lot of it went right by me, and I'd have to re-read it to get anything out of it. But yeah, lots of smart people have lots of good things to say about her, and I probably ought to at least re-acquaint myself before I go on the market, if not for the dissertation.

And that's the tough part. I mean, I haven't even got a flippin prospectus yet, and I'm already happily piling stuff on the reading list like it's a fire that's gotta last me twenty winters. I find it so easy to tell myself I don't yet know enough, and so hard to tell myself to stop reading and start writing. Every night. And maybe that's what the Tutor means when he talks about the tentativity of my "academic" style.
